content.text:
Source investigated was GitHub Issues in verified repository `max-sixty/worktrunk`. No writes performed.

Searched all issue states with `prune`, `prune "age"`, `prune "dirty"`, and `"prune" "rebase"`. Read full bodies and comments for #1818, #948, #1806, #3842, and #3004.

Direct evidence:

- [#1818](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/issues/1818), reported March 30, 2026, describes precisely a squash merge followed by edits on main causing merge conflicts. Reporter says `wt list` shows X and prune reports “No merged worktrees to remove.” A [bot comment](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/issues/1818#issuecomment-4158313922) identifies conservative integration detection on `merge-tree` conflicts and links proposed patch-id fallback #1820. Issue closed April 2. This establishes a historical failure mode, not that installed v0.81 still has it.
- [#948 maintainer comment](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/issues/948#issuecomment-3867857918), February 8, asks “but what if someone has just a started a session on a new worktree?” This directly establishes the safety concern behind an age guard. Its [closing bot comment](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/issues/948#issuecomment-3971108083) says `--min-age`, then default 1h, addressed that concern.
- [#3004 bot comment](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/issues/3004#issuecomment-4641642253), June 7, instead states default minimum age is one day. It says candidates show `_` or `⊂` and names `wt step prune --min-age=0s`. Use installed help to resolve the historical default discrepancy.
- [#1806 maintainer comment](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/issues/1806#issuecomment-4154645847) explains why this remains a separate command. He wants `wt remove` options terse and prune adds options. Bot comments identify the bulk command as `wt step prune`.
- [#3842](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/issues/3842) explains that ahead/diff-looking counts can remain substantial for a squash-merged branch marked integrated. Its body is explicitly attributed to Claude Code on behalf of the maintainer. This supports avoiding ahead/behind counts alone as an integration verdict.

Contradictions and limits:

- #1818 contains bot discussion saying prune preserves the branch ref. #3004 says prune deletes branches too. Those bot statements conflict, so neither should override installed implementation/help.
- No issue directly established why these particular Exposed branches are unrecognized in v0.81.
- Dirty-worktree searching returned related safety issues and older discussion, but I found no authoritative issue statement sufficient to establish the installed dirty-worktree rule.
- No bounded-search result directly established a rebase-history-specific prune bug. The confirmed historical analogue concerns squash merges and subsequent conflicting edits.

Additional lead for the source-control investigator is [PR #1820](https://github.com/max-sixty/worktrunk/pull/1820), linked by #1818. I did not inspect it because this investigation was restricted to issues.
